name: Sexual content (all-ages and family-friendly)
description: A strict list for groups where minors are present by design. Flags explicit language, kink vocabulary, adult-content advertising and innuendo an 18+ venue would never care about. Expect a higher flag rate than the 18+ list -- that is the intent. Do not enable this alongside the 18+ list; pick one.

rules.note: Explicit anatomical and crude terms. 'Dick' is also a given name and a surname (Philip K. Dick, Dick Grayson) and 'balls' is ordinary in sports -- both will produce dismissals in a gaming or comics community. 'Ass' alone is deliberately absent: it is too common in ordinary speech and in place names, and word boundaries do not save you from the dismissal volume.

Explicit sex acts. 'Anal' will match inside no other English word at a boundary, but watch for 'analysis' if your matcher's boundary handling is loose -- report it if you see that. 'Cum' as Latin ('magna cum laude', 'cum laude') is the one genuine false positive; an academic bio is where you will see it.

Pornography sites and genres. In an all-ages group these are a rules problem regardless of intent. 'Doujin' also covers entirely non-sexual fan works, including music albums and games, which is the main dismissal you will see in an anime community.

Adult-content markers of any kind. In an all-ages group the marker itself is the problem -- it advertises adult content to an audience that includes children, whether or not the content is reachable from here. Note that 'minors DNI' and 'MDNI' are not in this pattern: those are people trying to keep minors away, and flagging them would punish the responsible behaviour.

Erotic roleplay, the VRChat term. The noneOf list excludes refusals -- 'no ERP' is a boundary, not an offer -- and the business-software meaning, which will come up in any group with working adults in it.

Kink vocabulary. Nothing here is illegal or abusive and much of it is ordinary among adults -- the reason it is flagged in an all-ages group is audience, not content. 'Kinky' is also used about hair texture, which is a real and slightly awkward false positive worth knowing about before you message someone.

These words are near-useless alone and this rule shows why the combination type exists. 'Sub' is subscribe, subreddit, substitute and submarine. 'Switch' is a Nintendo console -- in a VRChat group, overwhelmingly so. 'Dom' is short for Dominic and for the DOM in web development. 'Daddy' is a parent. Only the pairing with an explicit solicitation phrase is flagged, and the console and subscription senses are excluded outright. If this rule still generates noise in your group, turn it off rather than tuning it -- the signal is thin.

Statements of arousal. 'Horny' is also used as a self-mocking joke by a great many people who mean nothing by it ('horny for pasta'), and 'down bad' has drifted to mean generally unlucky. Review, not high, for that reason -- but in a family-friendly group it is still a conversation.

rules.regex: \b(?:netflix and chill|dtf|wap|smash or pass|hit it and quit|back ?shots|beat it up|no ?bitches|bussy)\b
rules.note: Innuendo that an 18+ venue would ignore entirely and a family-friendly group probably will not. Recorded rather than flagged because most of it is teenage joking rather than solicitation. The right response to almost every one of these is a quiet word, not a sanction.

Recorded only. 'Snack' and 'smash' both have completely ordinary meanings -- food and Super Smash Bros, which in a VRChat gaming group is constant -- so treat matches as context for other flags rather than as findings. If 'smash' is generating dozens of dismissals a day, disable this rule.

Aubergine, peach or honeypot immediately followed by droplets, a tongue or lips. Emoji survive text normalisation untouched, so they are a common way to write innuendo past a word filter. Adjacency is required -- a bio that happens to mention both fruit and water will not match.

Roleplay action text in asterisks, restricted to explicitly sexual verbs. Non-sexual emotes (*waves*, *hugs*, *purrs*) are not matched. In a roleplay-heavy community this will fire on in-character text -- decide as a group whether in-character counts, because the tool cannot tell.

Recorded. 'Body count' means number of sexual partners in one usage and number of kills in another, and in a gaming community the second is far more common. The gaming senses are excluded; what is left is still mild enough to only record.

Partner-seeking in a group that is not for that. Harmless in itself and often just lonely, but in an all-ages space it is the entry point for adults approaching minors, which is why it is worth seeing. The 'gf' trigger also covers 'bf' variants in most matchers; if yours does not, add a sibling rule.

This rule is documentation and will never fire in practice, because no profile contains its allOf phrase. It exists to record a design decision where moderators will see it: stating a sexual orientation or gender identity is NOT sexual content, and nothing in this list treats it as such. 'I'm gay' is not a sexual statement; 'looking to hook up' is. If your group is tempted to add orientation words to this list, that is the line to hold.

Plain sexual vocabulary. 'Sex' appears in legitimate contexts constantly -- 'sex education', 'same-sex', 'sex assigned at birth', 'Middlesex' -- so expect dismissals and read the fragment. In an educational community, turn this rule off; it will fight the curriculum.

Adult-industry work advertised in an all-ages space. This is a placement problem, not a judgement on the work. 'Escort' also has a car and a military meaning; 'SW' is also short for software and Star Wars, which is why it requires the suffix.

Explicit furry content. The furry fandom is overwhelmingly non-sexual and 'fursona' alone means nothing at all -- flagging it would be both wrong and a good way to lose a large part of your membership. An explicit term must appear alongside it, and self-declared SFW accounts are excluded.
Sex products. A sexual-health educator's bio will match every one of these, which is exactly why an educational group should either disable this rule or expect to dismiss it with a shrug.
Scoped to the nameplate. 'Breeding' is ordinary in farming, animal husbandry and Pokemon, so this is scoped tightly rather than run against bios where those contexts live.

Display-name scope, no reclaimed-use allowance. In an adult venue 'slut' is reclaimed by plenty of people about themselves; in a family-friendly group it is over a child's head in every screenshot. 'Hoe' is also a garden tool, which is a real if slightly comic dismissal in a gardening world.

Unusually, this IS flagged in an all-ages list, and for the opposite reason to everywhere else. These markers are protective and responsible -- but an account carrying them is telling you it has adult content attached, and it has joined a group full of minors. The flag is not 'this member did something wrong', it is 'this account and this group are a poor fit'. Lead with that when you contact them.
'DM me for fun' is the standard euphemism. The noneOf list removes the many innocent uses of 'fun', which is one of the most common words in any bio. Even so, expect this one to need dismissals.

Requests for photographic 'age verification' sent person-to-person, which is a standard pretext for obtaining images. Legitimate verification is done by the platform or by group staff through an established process, not by a stranger in a DM.

Deliberate misspellings that survive normalisation because they are not simple character substitutions -- doubled letters, dropped letters, spelled-out numbers. Normalisation handles leetspeak; it does not handle someone typing 'pron' on purpose. That is what this rule is for.
ASCII genitalia. Crude rather than dangerous, and almost always a child testing what they can get away with, which is useful information in itself. Recorded, not flagged.

Telling a young person they are mature for their age is a documented grooming approach, and in an all-ages group it is worth seeing even when it is meant kindly. Overlaps with the underage-risk list on purpose; enable both in an all-ages group.
Dating and hookup services linked from an all-ages profile. Mostly a placement problem again -- the apps themselves are unremarkable for adults.
Advertising explicit roleplay. Roleplay itself is a huge and mostly wholesome part of VRChat, so the explicit marker is required and self-declared SFW accounts are excluded.

Inviting members into private instances. Entirely normal between friends; worth seeing in an all-ages group when it is advertised publicly to strangers, because a private instance has no witnesses. Low confidence, hence review.
